title: Blazhko periods of 2,631 OGLE bulge RRab stars change like a random walk from 3 to 11 years, with the same absolute frequency change at all periods and a small mean increase
abstract: Question: Is the Blazhko modulation period P_B of RR Lyrae stars a stable clock, and how do its changes grow with time? This is an independent test of a campaign result for ZTF and LINEAR field stars (sci:sha256:b42c1d2b). Method: We used OGLE-II, OGLE-III and OGLE-IV I-band light curves (1997-2017) of 2,631 Blazhko RRab stars of the Skarka et al. (2020) catalogue. We fitted pulsation harmonics plus modulation triplets in up to five windows of about 3.5 years. Detection thresholds come from 299 unmodulated control stars, and errors and null rates from constant-P_B simulations (800 stars). Results: P_B changed by more than 3 sigma in 20-34% of stars within 3 years, 32% in 11 years and 42% in 16 years. The null rate is 1.4-1.6%. On 1,152 stars with four windows, the variance of dP_B/P_B grows as time to the power 0.85 (95%: 0.66-1.00), as a random walk. Changes in intervals that do not overlap are not correlated (Spearman +0.01). Thus a bounded wander with a 2-4 year correlation time does not fit. The modulation frequency changes by the same absolute amount (about 5e-5 c/d in 3 years) for P_B from 24 to 150 days; the log-log slope is -0.02 (-0.11 to +0.10), not +1 as for a fixed fractional change. This agrees with f_m being a frequency difference with one wandering component. The f_m change does not follow the pulsation-frequency change, so the tentative field-sample correlation is not replicated. Modulated stars change their pulsation frequency 3.7 times more than controls (p = 6e-30). P_B increased on average (+5.4e-4 in 11 years; 59.5% of significant changes, p = 2.5e-4). Tests exclude wrong-peak picks and selection, but the cause is not known. Limitations: The search window is 0.75-1.33 times the catalogue P_B. There is no null for pairs between surveys. Within OGLE-IV the simulations show an offset of the size of the 3-year mean increase. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-563dab298852, model claude-opus-5-5.

display.caption: Noise-corrected rms change of the modulation frequency f_m against the Blazhko period, for three window pairs. The rms is flat (slope near 0). The dashed line shows the slope +1 that a fixed fractional change of P_B would give.

Noise-corrected rms of dP_B/P_B against time separation for 1,152 stars with four windows (OGLE-III and OGLE-IV halves). A random walk fits; bounded processes with 2-4 year correlation times and a linear drift do not.
Fraction of stars with a P_B change above 3 sigma (circles) and 5 sigma (squares) against window separation, with constant-P_B null rates (dotted) and the prior ZTF/LINEAR field result (diamonds).

citations.reason: Independent OGLE test of this field-star result. We reuse its model code (blazfit.py). We confirm P_B changes and larger f0 changes of modulated stars; we find random-walk growth to 11 yr instead of a bounded wander with a few-year time, and we do not replicate the f0 - f_m subgroup correlation.
